$comment: Firestore contract for the Breach & Patch Range. Every agent reads and writes ONLY through this shape. The dashboard reads the same collections via real-time listeners. This file is the single source of truth for the data contract: agents/breach_range/shared/schema.py and web/lib/firestore.ts must both match it. Timestamps are Firestore serverTimestamp() on write, surfaced to clients as ISO 8601.

graph.$comment: One live document, id 'current'. Recon rewrites it each round; Attacker flags nodes reachable; Referee corrects those flags after verification; Defender's applied patch removes edges on the next Recon pass.

score.note: verified-reachable misconfigs this round; the number the scoreboard plots

events.$comment: Append-only. One doc per agent action. Nothing an agent does lives only in its head; if it happened, it is an event. This collection IS the audit trail after the demo. Never update or delete an event; corrections are new events.

target.note: node id, edge id, or path id the action concerns

payload.note: action-specific; e.g. a Path for attacker.claim, a unified diff string for defender.proposed

result.note: short human-readable outcome, e.g. 'reachable via MC-01 -> MC-02' or 'rejected: deny policy blocks token creation'

example.result: public bucket leaks CI key, key escalates to owner

rounds.$comment: Optional but cheap, and it makes the scoreboard trivial: one doc per completed round. The descending score line reads straight off scoreAfter.

patchApplied.note: path id the Defender closed this round, or null

Node.id: string, stable, formatted '<kind>:<shortname>' so edges reference it
Node.name: string, the real GCP resource name
Node.reachable: bool, set by Attacker, corrected by Referee
Node.fromMisconfig: string|null, the seeded misconfig id if this node exists because of one
Node.labels: object, free-form facts Recon read (roles, iamPublic, cidr, etc.)

Edge.relation: enum<Relation>, an allow-relationship only; deny is never modelled by design

Path.edges: array<edge id>, ordered from startNode to targetNode

invariants: Only the Referee writes status 'verified' or 'rejected'. The Attacker only writes 'claimed'.
score on graph/current must equal the count of nodes reachable=true that the Referee has verified this round.
The Defender writes 'defender.proposed' and 'approval.requested', then waits. 'defender.applied' is written only after an 'approval.granted' event exists for the same target.
